core_meaning.short_meaning: The cooing of a dove; a gentle melodious sound
core_meaning.primary_meaning: Hadil corresponds to the Arabic form هديل and is glossed in this record as “The cooing of a dove; a gentle melodious sound.” The record associates the form with root ه د ل (h-d-l). The lexical gloss describes the word-form; Qur’anic occurrence, religious recommendation, popularity, and a name-bearer’s character are separate claims and are not established by this gloss alone.
core_meaning.literal_meaning: The cooing of a dove; a gentle melodious sound
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: Hadil corresponds to the Arabic form هديل (Arabic root ه د ل (h-d-l); هديل (Hadīl)). Its core sense is the cooing of a dove; melodious sound. Hadil is a transliteration of Arabic هديل (Hadīl) 'the cooing of a dove; a gentle melodious sound'. The source gloss 'delicate, tender, agile' is an extrapolation of the dove image rather than the lexical meaning; same word as hadeel.
